title: Intercept Relief Months for Reinstated Plans — Benefit Overpayment Accounts Desk Guidance
content:
A claimant whose federal or state tax refund was intercepted for an overpayment on Benefit Overpayment Accounts within the intercept look-back months before the handling date receives intercept relief months added to the reinstatement months of a reinstated repayment plan.

## The rule the desk applies

The intercept look-back is 12 months: an intercept counts when the whole months from its booking date on the overpayment's ledger to the handling date are fewer than 12. Both Treasury Offset Program intercepts of a federal tax refund and state tax refund intercepts count, and their amounts are totalled.

| Intercepts for the overpayment within the 12-month look-back | Relief months added |
|---|---|
| Totalling at least USD 1000.00 (the large-intercept amount) | 6, the large intercept extension |
| Totalling more than zero but less than USD 1000.00 | 3, the small intercept extension |
| No intercept | None |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical totals)

| Total intercepted in the look-back | Relief months |
|---|---|
| USD 1000.00 | 6 |
| USD 999.99 | 3 |
| USD 40.00 | 3 |
| Nothing | 0 |

## Questions at the desk

**An intercept was booked 14 months ago. Does it count?** No; it is outside the 12-month look-back.

**Two intercepts of USD 600.00 each fall within the look-back. Which row applies?** Their total, USD 1200.00, is at least USD 1000.00, so 6 relief months are added.
